  • A fix, when safe, is a button beside the row (Use claude, Remove), written to the file; Open line N opens the document there.

Errors (each ends "The loop won't start until this is fixed."):

Message (start) Fix No agent called `codx`. Did you mean `codex`? A by: that names no agent, or a box's word that is its by said short (plan: codx); the row suggests the nearest `swep` is not something `search` takes: it is a search (sweep, ...), a list of phases or `module:Class` A word the key does not take; the row lists the ones it does and suggests the nearest A document does not say its `id`: it is its folder's name Rename the folder instead `statement` must be a non-empty string: what is to be made Say what is to be made REFUSED: `problem.yaml` names 1 path the loop folder does not have (the check's text, with what the folder holds) Add the listed file to the folder, or fix the key that names it 'notes.md' is not a file or folder beside ... (knowledge.library) Add the file, or list what is there `check` is never delegated to an agent: it establishes facts check and measure are commands only `{...}` is not something `design` takes: it is "flux" (FluxAgent), {run: [...]}, {catalog: [...]} or {agent: ...} One form only `flow.design.command` is not a key of a document: a command a document runs is said `run:` (and search's, baseline's, an estimate's, an agent of your own's by: {command: ...}) Say run: flow.design.agent.session is `pass` (one session per design until it is admitted ...) or `keep` Write pass or keep, or remove session from design `dse` is `search` / `extract` is `knowledge: {insights: {by: rules}}` Old names: search and knowledge.insights Who works it is by Write knowledge: {by: claude} or {by: off} `budget.parallel` is a key of an older document, which this Flux no longer reads: open the document with Flux e7a0f9cba, which says what became of it, and export it again (any key) A moved key (budget.parallel, flow.knowledge.digest, flow.measure.<stage>.command, parts:, ...): Flux e7a0f9cba names its replacement. A key for something gone (cache:, brief:, knowledge.sheet) is a warning, ignored; a retired one (budget.finalists, flow.calibrate) warns "does nothing in this Flux: it was retired (remove it)" Generator says {nope}, which is neither a knob of `flow.search.space` (...) nor the loop's (...) A misspelled placeholder, or a knob not in the space `flow.search.space` knobs (...) are said by no command Name a {knob} or {point} in a command, or generate with a command A stage needs `metrics` (...) or `metrics_re` Say what the stage prints `wavee` is not a setting of gradient (its settings: ...) (at search.method.gradient.wavee, a phase's at search.method[1].wavee) An option the search does not have; the message lists its settings (search settings) `critic` names the box's critic (flux or an agent), not a A check or a stage cannot be called critic: it names the box's critic `sweep` is a search, not an intent: `search: sweep` policy: names a policy, search: a search `explore` is an intent, not a search: `policy: explore` Say it under policy:; beside it search: names the algorithm `policy: tune` is the intent beside the phase's search: say the search too A phase says its search: {search: gradient, policy: tune} (or search: model) Its points are picked by a search (...) or proposed by FluxAgent or an agent (search.space) Add method: sweep (or another search), or by: flux `baseline` takes file OR command OR metrics One source per baseline not a task: `problem.yaml` is not a mapping of keys The file is a list or a single value; start from a new loop's document

A refused document never runs; Start shows the same message first.

docs.title: Searches
docs.text: What flow.search takes as a search. Search and agents explains when to use which.

docs.title: Space and seeds
docs.text:
flow.search is one form, {by: <who decides>, policy: <name>, method: <how the points are picked>, space: {...}}:

Said What runs nothing, or {by: rules} the rules pick each pass's direction and the kind of work, no AI {by: flux}, {by: tools}, {by: claude} FluxAgent, FluxAgent with its tools, an agent decides ({by: given} is the rules, under that name) {by: ..., policy: explore} (no space) the same, with that policy {method: sweep, space: {...}} that search walks the space; by beside it has no effect (a warning) {policy: explore, method: gradient, space: {...}} the search, with that policy {by: flux, space: {...}}, {by: claude, policy: explore, space: {...}} FluxAgent (or the agent) proposes the points, with that policy {run: ...} your own search (below)
  • Shorthand: search: explore is {policy: explore}, search: sweep {method: sweep}, search: claude {by: claude}; a list is {method: [...]}.
  • Refused: a space with nobody to pick its points; a search under policy: ("sweep is a search, not an intent: method: sweep"); a policy under method:.
  • A search without a space walks nothing.

A search tries points of a space of settings ("knobs"):

search:                                             # under flow:
  method: {gradient: {steps: 16, patience: 2}}     # or: method: gradient
  space:
    algorithm: [list_sieve, slice_sieve, odd_sieve]
    wheel: {values: [0, 1], when: {algorithm: [list_sieve]}}   # only moves for list_sieve
    prefetch:                                       # a component: prefetch.on, .distance, .degree
      optional: true
      distance: [1, 2, 4]
      degree: [1, 2]
    variant: {values: [baseline], from: "variants/*.py"}       # plus file stems found at load
  seeds:
    - {algorithm: list_sieve, wheel: 0}            # measured first; the first seed is home
  • space: each knob is an ordered, non-empty list of scalar choices. Order numeric choices: local searches step to neighbours.
    • A map with values may add when: {knob: choice or [choices]} (moves only then; else its first choice) and from: glob (adds matching file stems, read at every load).
    • A map with neither is a component: knobs component.knob; optional: true adds component.on. They reach commands through {point} only ({component.knob} is not substituted).
  • seeds: measured first; a missing knob takes its first choice.
  • A space must reach a command: a command names a {knob} or {point}, or the generator is a command or catalog. With a model or agent generator, a space only tunes settings.

docs.title: Searches
docs.text: method Options and defaults sweep batch_size: 0 (the whole walk at once) montecarlo samples: 24, batch_size: 8, seed: 0 gradient steps: 16, wave: 0 (all moves), patience: 1, budget: 0 (no cap), reach: adjacent (or any) anneal steps: 32, seed: 0, temperature: 1.0, cooling: 0.9 genetic population: 8, generations: 6, seed: 0, mutation: 0.3 pareto budget: 24, wave: 6, reference: [], scale: [], reach: adjacent; needs two objectives: with one, the search says so in the log and walks nothing (no search, by: flux) FluxAgent proposing points: batch_size: 4, rounds: 8, shown: 40; written {by: flux, ...} (model, its old name, too) or {by: claude, ...} for an agent control keep: []: compare home with only these incumbent knobs kept a list, phases phases in order, each {search: ..., policy: ..., ...its options} (default gradient; search: model FluxAgent proposing the phase's points); {phases: {phases: [...]}} is the long form; phases do not nest module:Class a search policy class of your own, beside the document adaptive, explore, improve, tune, finetune, variations Not searches: said policy:, which sets the search's emphasis (default adaptive) run Your own search: search: {run: ..., timeout_s: 600} (contract)

docs.title: Options every search takes
docs.text:
Option Purpose name A label knobs Move only these (globs such as prefetch.*) hold Keep these fixed (globs too) metric, direction Its own target; default the first objective floor {metric, at} or {metric, keep, above}: designs below it are refused margin Minimum improvement, default 0 policy Its emphasis, as above
  • batch is another name for batch_size: how many designs one pass carries (what a pass carries).
  • An unknown option is refused where written (flow.search.method[1].wavee).
  • budget.tools_at_once: how many of a pass's designs are made and checked at once.
  • A finished walk does not stop an open-ended run: cap passes at Start, or with budget.passes.

docs.title: Write a loop with an agent
docs.text:
Describe the loop, attach your files, and an agent writes it: the document, its checks and measurements, and a golden model where one fits. The author is FluxAgent or a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or one your server adds). Nothing runs until you start it.

Try it first in the Preview app: create a loop step by step starts with this way.

docs.title: New loop › Agent
docs.text:
On the Loops list, New loop › Agent. The page has four stages:

  1. Ask: name, agent, what the loop should do, and its files (drop them, or a folder or a .zip, on the form). It can use names the machine the agent runs on (Machines); with none, no machine and no draft.
    • Hide from AI on a file keeps it from every agent (a gate's tests, say).
    • Ask me when unclear (on by default): the agent asks before drafting.
    • Thinking and Effort work as in Chat.
  2. Drafting: the agent's conversation, live, as in Chat.
    • Below it: the files it wrote (written, yours or removed; a lock on hidden ones), the check's last word, its tool calls and checks run.
    • Its questions show as one card.
    • Draft refused? Try again, or type a note in the message box (Enter sends).
  3. Review: its decisions by configurator step, each with its reason. Keep, Change (opens the configurator at that step) or Keep the rest. A change asked in the message box shows as a diff.
  4. Ready: the draft's check (as Settings › Problem › Check). Make loop, or Open in Configurator first. Run one pass first starts one ordinary pass to the deepest stage.

Notes:

  • The draft is a loop from Drafting on. This browser remembers it; you can come back.
  • The agent starts from a new loop's files (a README and library/). It checks its draft and repairs it until the check passes; a coding agent also proves its gate on a sample design before handing over. It never runs the loop itself.
  • When it ends, its changes come back exactly, removals and renames included. Scratch files never come back.
  • Settings › Problem › Agent on an existing loop asks an agent to change it the same way.

docs.title: Ask me when unclear
docs.text:
On, the agent asks before writing anything:

  • what your ask leaves open: objectives and goals, limits (clock, area, latency, budget), measurement stages and tools, which file is the spec or golden model, who designs;
  • up to four questions at once, each with choices and one marked Recommended;
  • the card offers a chip per question, You decide, a free answer, and a timer (10 minutes, then the agent decides);
  • its decisions say which answer decided what;
  • a long question folds behind Show all, never cut.

When revising, it asks only if the change is ambiguous. Off, it asks nothing and records each assumption in its decisions.

docs.title: One session per loop
docs.text:
A coding agent (OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex) keeps one session per loop. Every later job on the loop resumes it: a change in Review, Try again, a note, an edit from Settings › Problem › Agent. Two loops never share a session.

The conversation's first line says which: Session: resumed session (turn 3) or Session: new session (why). A new session starts when:

  • the loop has none yet;
  • you picked another agent, or its model changed;
  • the loop's folder moved;
  • the agent cannot resume (session gone, or context truly full).

A new session starts from the whole brief and the loop's files.

docs.title: When a turn is cut off
docs.text: A job ends when the agent ends its turn. A turn that times out or errors continues in the same session, a few times (three by default). Then the job ends as The agent did not finish: its files are kept, and Try again continues. Stop ends a job the same way.

docs.title: FluxAgent as the author
docs.text:
• Reads and writes the draft's folder only: no path outside it, no hidden name (.x), no path hidden from AI.
  • Checks the draft with Flux's own check and fixes it until it passes. A draft still refused comes back to it, a few times.
  • Runs nothing, so it does not prove the gate on a sample design.
  • Keeps no session between jobs.

docs.title: Check what it wrote
docs.text:
The author's loop is a first draft. Before a long run, check:

  • Checks: do they test what you care about, on enough inputs?
  • Measurements: right workload, right stage, tools_at_once: 1 for timings?
  • Objectives: the limit you meant, in the right direction?
  • Run one pass (Run one pass first on Ready, or Start with one pass) and read its results.

See Configure and Knowledge, skills, hidden paths.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Flux runs as a web server: you install it once, then everything happens in the browser. It is a Python package (Python 3.11 or newer); the hardware tools and the sandbox are optional.

To try the web app first, open the Preview app: create a loop step by step, then a tour of the app, or the tour alone.

docs.title: Install and start the server
docs.text:
The source is not public: ask the maintainer for access. From its folder (here flux-repo):

cd flux-repo
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -e "./flux[web]"
source .venv/bin/activate
flux user add me --admin
flux serve
  • flux user add makes the first account; run it as the user who should own the loops' files.
  • flux serve prints its address (default http://127.0.0.1:8765/). Open it and sign in. Every other account is made in the web app (Admin › People › Users).
  • Before the first Start, add a machine to run the loops: the server itself runs none. The usual one is its own host -- Admin › Runtime › Machines › + Add machine, Role This server's host, and the line it shows run as root on the server (Machines). Until then Start says "loop: no machine".
  • A server started by hand is for trying Flux. For a team, install the system service.

Next: the Web app tour, then your first loop.

docs.title: Sandbox
docs.text:
Checks, runs and agents run inside a container. Install Podman (rootless, preferred) or Docker on the server's machine. Without either, a start stops with the sandbox needs Podman or Docker.

For code you trust, an admin can turn the sandbox off for one loop (Settings › Advanced). What the sandbox sees and reaches: Run, stop, resume › Sandbox.

docs.title: Hardware tools
docs.text:
Hardware loops need Verilator, Yosys, OpenROAD and other tools. Flux's Nix shell has them all, and the coding agents Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode (Models and agents).

  1. Install Nix.
  2. Add experimental-features = nix-command flakes to ~/.config/nix/nix.conf.
  3. Start the server from the shell (the first entry may build or download tools):
cd flux-repo/flux
nix develop --accept-flake-config
flux serve

The shell puts Flux on PATH: no pip install inside it.

docs.title: System service
docs.text:
A team server runs as a system service, under its own flux account. As root, from flux/:

sudo python3 scripts/install-service.py --with-worker -- --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8765

The installer is safe to run again: each step already done is skipped. It makes the flux account, lets it use Nix and the binary caches, prepares rootless Podman (sub-ids, linger, cgroup controllers), clones the code, writes /etc/flux/service.env with your proxy settings, installs and enables the service, and makes the first admin (it asks a password). --with-worker also joins this host as the machine the loops run on (flux-worker.service, the same account, the server's own disk: This server's host); without it, add the host from Admin › Runtime › Machines before the first Start. When something it cannot change is missing, it says what and stops. --dry-run reports what is there and what is missing, and writes nothing.

What Where Account flux, a system user Code its own clone, /opt/flux/src Web data /var/lib/flux/web Caches /var/cache/flux Settings /etc/flux/service.env, one NAME=value a line

Afterwards, everything is in the web app: updates in Admin › Server › Version, agents' logins in Account › Agents, backups in Admin › Server › Maintenance.

docs.title: Models and agents
docs.text: A loop whose designs come from a script needs no model. Otherwise set FluxAgent's endpoint and the coding agents in the web app: Models and agents.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• First loop: a complete loop in the web app, Python only.
  • Write a loop with an agent: describe it, an agent writes it.
  • Create a loop step by step in the Preview app.

docs.title: VS Code
docs.text: Run a loop on the folder you have open in VS Code, on your own machine, and keep it on the Flux server: Live, Results, notes and Stop work from the web as for any loop. The loop's agents use your machine's own logins (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode as you have them).

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
The extension brings no Flux of its own: once you sign in, it downloads the Flux that runs your loops, and the Python it runs on, from your Flux server. The machine where the folder is needs only:

  • your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode), installed and logged in -- its VS Code extension may be enough (below);
  • the tools your loop's checks run (compilers, simulators): its steps run on this machine, with your own PATH -- a step's python3 is yours; Flux adds only its own flux and fluxpreset.

No Python, no Nix, no Podman, no containers: the machine is the loop's boundary. It runs Linux on x86_64 (x64) or aarch64 (Arm64) with glibc 2.27 or later -- most distributions, WSL, dev containers, a Remote-SSH host from VS Code on Windows or macOS; not Alpine (musl).

  1. On the Flux web, Account › Machines › VS Code extension: Download.
  2. In VS Code: Extensions › ⋯ › Install from VSIX… and pick that file.
  3. Sign in. The first time, a notification shows Flux downloading from the server (some 45 MB).

On a machine it does not run on, the Flux view says what it runs on.

After the server is updated, the extension fetches the server's new Flux by itself and moves to it once no loop is running here (a window's folder or another's): a run in progress finishes on the one it started with. The move is one handover: the old worker ends, the new one starts and has 90 seconds to connect and stand; a new Flux that does not start, connect or stand gives way to the one before, which runs again, and the bottom line says why until Refresh tries it again. A worker that ended before the move is moved all the same: an update never leaves this machine without one. A run here never holds the server's update: while the server restarts the run goes on, and the run reaches the new server once it is back (its journal, its record, its end). Live says which Flux it runs: "runtime 3581a0c2". Without the server, the Flux it has keeps working. The line at the bottom of the Flux view says which code runs here: code 3581a0c ✓ when it is the server's, updating to … while it moves to a new one.

The extension updates itself too: install it by hand once, and after a server update it installs the server's new one and says Flux updated: Restart Flux to use it.

To update now, use Refresh in the Flux view's ⋯ menu: it fetches the server's new Flux and extension at once and says Flux is up to date when there is nothing new.

docs.title: Your agents
docs.text:
Flux finds each agent's program on this machine, first found first:

  1. a program the loop's problem.yaml names for it (bin, or an agent of its own);
  2. the agent's VS Code extension, when it carries the agent's program: Flux uses that program;
  3. the program on the machine's PATH.

Their sign-in is the agent's own: logging in from the Claude Code or Codex panel logs in the agent your loop runs. When neither is found, the graph's head and the agent's row in its box's section of problem.yaml's form say so (hover it for how to install it). The row says where each agent was found ("Claude Code (VS Code extension)", PATH, this document's).

FluxAgent is the server's: its steps ask the endpoint set on the server (Admin or Account › Agents › FluxAgent) through the server, so nothing has to run on your machine for it.

docs.title: Sign in
docs.text:
1. On the Flux web, Account › Machines › New VS Code code: give it a name (this VS Code's, such as laptop) and copy the code. It is shown once.
  2. In VS Code, open the Flux view: its Setup section says what is next. Set the server opens Flux: Server (flux.server) in Settings: the server's address, such as http://flux.example:8080 (Settings marks an address that is not one).
  3. Sign in with a VS Code code (in Setup, or from the Command Palette) and paste it.

A code signs in one VS Code, once, and with it every folder you open in that VS Code: you sign in once. The code is used up (pasted again, it is refused); a code nobody used expires after a day.

Once signed in, VS Code stays signed in -- across reloads, restarts, and in VS Code in a browser from any browser -- until you revoke it or sign out. It only attaches, creates, starts, stops and notes your own loops, and downloads the server's Flux; everything else stays on the web.

Account › Machines lists the codes not used yet (Revoke one you no longer need), and each signed-in VS Code as one machine under the code's name, tagged VS Code, its Loops column naming the loops attached there -- running, idle, or folder not open (Machines). Revoke on it signs that VS Code out and refuses its machine's key; its loops stay yours. Sign out in VS Code signs it out from there, for every folder; the machine stays.

A machine revoked (or removed on the server) stops, and VS Code says so; revoked, VS Code is signed out there too. Sign in again and Attach (or the notice's Attach): it joins anew under the same name. Nothing to delete by hand.

docs.title: Attach
docs.text:
Open your project's folder and choose Attach this folder in Setup (or on the status bar). Its loop lives in the folder's .flux/: problem.yaml, the loop's scripts, its results and what its runs write. Its commands reach your project's files as {project}/... (Document). Flux:

  • sends the .flux folder once to the server as a loop of yours, named after your folder;
  • adds /.flux/ to your folder's .gitignore: the loop stays out of your repository;
  • adds this VS Code to Account › Machines as one machine named after your code (the first folder attached joins it; the next ones use it), and makes it the loop's home: the loop runs there from now on. The machine runs the loops of the folders open in your VS Code windows, several at once (one run a loop); a window closed stops its loop's run, and the last window closed ends the worker.

Until the loop is attached, Setup offers Attach this folder; a folder with no loop yet offers New loop… (below); the status bar names the same step. The Loop view shows once Flux is on this machine (after you sign in), and once the loop is attached Setup goes. A folder whose problem.yaml is at its root offers to move it into .flux/ (its commands then say {project}/... where they said {home}/...), or to attach it as it is.

A loop that hides files from its agents which someone else may have hidden cannot be attached: on your machine they would not be hidden from you.

The loop keeps its name in .flux/: rename your project's folder and it is still the same loop. To rename the loop itself, stop it and change its Name at the top of problem.yaml's form (or choose Rename loop in the Flux view's menu): it is renamed on the server and in your folder, its results with it.

docs.title: The loop in the sidebar
docs.text:
The Flux view draws your folder's loop as one graph, top to bottom: Setup, Search, Design, Check, Measure, Choose, the Run strip and the Knowledge chips. AI marks a box an agent or FluxAgent works. Check and Measure are folded, as Live's graph draws them: one box with how many checks (or measurements) it holds and a thin bar for each -- in the box's colour when it passed in its latest run, red when it failed, amber when it passed after failing earlier in the pass, pulsing while it runs, grey while it waits or has not run yet, outlined when the checks stopped before it. Point at a bar for its check and its command; click it for its section of the form, or the box for the group's. The chevron (›) opens the group into its checks in order (or its stages, a stage's cutoff on the arrow after it), each with its own buttons and +; Flux remembers which groups you opened for each loop. A box's corner says how its last work went: a ✓ or ✗, or a turning ring while it works. Its head says where the loop stands in one word, the same as the status bar -- Running, Stopping, Stopped, Ended or Failed (hover it for why) -- its pass (re-measure pass for an R pass, which is not counted among the passes), for how long, its lanes, and the best design so far against your first goal, with Results to open the loop's Results in your browser (every design, compare, star, accept). When designs were measured before a change to how a stage measures them -- you edited its script, say -- a line says how many and what changed, as the web's Overview does, with Re-measure…: it asks, then measures them again (by the running loop before its next pass, else by a run of its own). Under it, a line for each agent that is not ready here, every agent Design takes turns with included -- "codex · not logged in here · Log in… · Test again" (hover it for the boxes that wait) -- Log in… opens a terminal running the agent's own login; it is tested again when the terminal closes. An agent is asked about its login by its own program -- the one your agents: names with bin:, so a build of OpenCode or Codex under another name counts once its own login works -- and the line says what is wrong in a few words: not installed, not logged in, or not answering; hover it for the agent's own words. The loop runs here as you, with your own logins, so Start waits only for a program that is missing or does not run: an agent whose own program says it is not logged in is said with Log in… and Start runs it anyway, and one whose login Flux cannot see is ready.

problem.yaml has two faces in one tab, as VS Code's Settings have: its text, and a form with every box as a section and their names down the side. Open as form (✎) and Open as text ({ }) in the editor's title bar switch between them, each landing where you were: on the box your cursor is in, or with the cursor at the lines of the section you were in. Click a box in the graph: the form opens at its section. The form writes problem.yaml in place -- your comments and the order of your keys stay -- and says saved to problem.yaml beside each change; what it does not edit it names under its fields, folded, with a link to its line. What you type or pick shows at once and stays while it is written; a change that cannot be written keeps your value and says why, beside the field. Undo, redo and the tab's unsaved dot are the editor's own; when the text has changes you have not saved, the form says so and shows them once you save. The text stays the default when you open problem.yaml; to open it as a form every time, set it in VS Code's Workbench › Editor Associations (problem.yaml → Flux form).

  • The Problem, at the top: the loop's Name (renames it), the Statement, the Artifact file, the Contract and the Environment: variables every process of the loop gets, its steps and its agents (env:), a row each; one Flux will not set says why at its row.
  • Agents: the agents problem.yaml defines for itself (agents:), each a section under it -- its Program (typed, or picked with the folder button; a program of your own its Command) with its state here beside it, and its Model. Under Fine-tune (folded): Interface (how the program is driven -- Default is what it says to --help, the words beside it say which, or why none; Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode an override; A program of my own turns it into a run: command), Arguments, Effort and Thinking (think), Timeout (seconds a turn), List command (models: {run: ...}, the command printing what Model offers; a list of names stays in problem.yaml) and Instructions (instructions:, text added to every brief the agent gets, after its kind's from Admin › Agents). + add an agent adds one; the boxes then name it.

  • Setup › Baseline: what is measured before pass 1 -- Off, The project as it is, A design file (picked with the folder button, relative to the loop's folder), A command and its timeout, or Known values (a metric, its value, its stage) -- and how its last run went: measured, failed and why, or standing unchanged.

  • A check or a stage: its name, its command -- a line of your own, a Preset (Flux's own checks and measurements that read the design's language and whose programs are on this machine, each written with its defaults: no Verilator here, no RTL preset offered; the one the step runs stays listed, and flux task check names a missing program), or one of your folder's VS Code tasks or launch configurations -- and its timeout. A check's Failures: Count (count_re: one capture group, the number of failures its output prints) or Each (fail_re: one match a failure) and the pattern of the one chosen; switching drops the other's. A stage's metrics and its Cutoffs, a row each (a metric, at least, at most or within a share of the best, its value): each must pass, else the design stops there; + cutoff adds one. + in Check or Measure (in the graph or the form) adds one (between two, with the + between them).

  • Each box shows its own buttons when you point at it or reach it with Tab: edit, go to its lines in problem.yaml, and remove (a check or a stage). Enter opens a box's section, Delete removes a check or a stage; both ask first.
  • Search, Design, Choose: who works it -- the rules, FluxAgent or an agent -- and, on the agent's row, its state on this machine with Log in… and Test again; its Model. Under Fine-tune (folded): Effort and Thinking; Timeout (seconds a turn, 1800 unsaid) -- on Design with Continues (times the agent's work goes on past it) and Grace (seconds of one last turn, a quarter of Timeout unsaid; budget's) beside it --; its Session (Setup's Plan, Search, Design, Choose): None (a new one each pass, on Design each design), Keep (kept pass after pass), and on Design Seed with every (passes). Design's Probe: whether its agent may try its file against the gate and the stages before handing it in (hover it for how often).
  • Design listing agents (by: [...]: a trunk's, or a passes' agents in turn) is a table, a row an entry of the list -- t1, t2 in trunk mode --: its Agent, Model (as any agent's: Default, its list, Other…, ⟳), Effort, Thinking, a dot for its state on this machine (hover it for the words), Test (⚗) and ×. The same agent twice is two rows (two trunks). A change writes that entry alone; what else the entry says (timeout_s, session, provider, …) stays as written and is counted on its row (+1, hover it for the keys -- a provider with its name). + agent lists the document's own agents, then the kinds installed here, each with its dot; the one picked is added at the end by its name (never FluxAgent: a list is coding agents'). The Fine-tune under the table is the box's own, every entry's default: Timeout, Continues, Grace, and in passes mode Session.
  • A Critic on Search, Check, Measure and Choose: Off, FluxAgent or an agent (picked as a box's); Search's and Choose's Rounds (1 to 5: how often the box answers its objections).
  • Choose's objectives: each metric higher or lower is better, or Tracked (not ranked) (no direction: shown, never ranked; the graph's Choose says it without an arrow); its goal and unit. A change rewrites that entry alone, its other keys (aggregate, tie, ...) kept.
  • A Model lists the models the agent offers on this machine, as its turns would run it -- for an agent of problem.yaml's own, its models: names or what its List command prints; one with its own Program and no models: lists none of its kind's, only (Claude Code's kind) its own service's when its settings name one (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL in its environment, the project's .claude/settings.local.json or .claude/settings.json, or its CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR's). Beside it, ⟳ asks again and a few words say how the listing went: 14 · 12:04 (how many, when), or no list · ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL unset (hover it for the whole: where Flux looked, or what the command said). Default writes none: the agent's definition's model, else your setting for its kind (Account › Agents), else the agent's own choice. A model set on a box wins over the definition's. Other… takes any name -- the agent answers for it at its first turn. A model the list says is one provider's reads GLM-V5.1 · wireless: picking it writes model: and provider: together (the agent's definition says the flag its CLI takes it by, provider_flag: --provider; Your own agents); picking a model listed with none removes provider:; Other… keeps whatever provider: is written; Default clears both.
  • Run: passes or trunk, Tools at once (the designs evaluated at once; unsaid, the agents + 1), passes, repairs, Pipeline (on by default: the next design drafted while the ones before are checked and measured; off writes pipeline: false, each session then waiting for its design's decision). Designs drafted at once is Design's table: an agent listed twice is two sessions. Knowledge: each part on or off, the paths hidden from the agents (hover a field for what it is).
  • In trunk mode the form shows only what a trunk runs: no Plan, no Prototype, no Repairs per design; Run says Designs for the hand-ins, and Pipeline as under Passes.

In problem.yaml's text, the box your cursor is in is selected in the graph -- in a folded group, the group and that check's bar -- and the editor's breadcrumb and Outline name it (Measure › synth).

problem.yaml stays yours: edit it by hand and the graph follows. Its mistakes show in Problems as you save. A part with a mistake is drawn in red with what is wrong; click it to go to its line. The head says how many problems there are, and Start waits until they are fixed. A new loop's graph is drawn before it is filled in: the head says what is left ("Add the statement first", "Add a check first", each with Open it to its place in the form), and Start waits for it. With Red Hat's YAML extension installed, problem.yaml also completes its keys and explains them as you type.

docs.title: Create
docs.text: A folder with no loop shows New loop… in Setup: pick where it starts -- the skeleton, your folder's VS Code tasks (pick which become checks and which stages), or describe it to an agent (say what the loop should make and how a design is checked and measured; the agent writes problem.yaml as New loop › Agent does). The server's New loop makes it, then it is brought into .flux/ and attached, and problem.yaml opens as a form at its Problem, the statement to write. Each AI box's agent and its state on this machine are on that box's row of the form and under the graph's head: log in to each before you start. A loop of yours with your folder's name on the server already is offered to bring here instead.

docs.title: Start
docs.text: Start in the Flux view's title bar (or the loop's Start on the web) runs it here; it is greyed while an agent is not ready on this machine, and the view's head says which. It asks how: Until stopped, A number of passes… (a trunk's: designs), Re-measure what is asked first (the R pass alone), Rerun the baseline first (pass 0 measured again, then until stopped), or Re-evaluate…, which opens the loop's Settings on the web to tick which designs. While it runs, the same graph lights up: the box at work, the designs in it (hover Design for the drafts at work), each check's and stage's bar, the checks' runs passed and failed after Check and the stages' after Measure, the best so far on Choose, the pass and its lanes on the Run strip. When it ends a notification says so -- how many passes and the best, or why it failed with Journal. A check or a stage whose command did not run at all (not a design failing it) shows in Problems at its line of problem.yaml until it runs again. Click a design to see its change in VS Code's diff editor; the Flux journal panel lists the steps at work and those that ended, offline too -- a failed one with why (hover it for the whole message); click a row whose words are cut to read them whole, and again to close it. A seed on a machine without Landlock says so beside its time. Until the run's first step -- this machine taking it, the sandbox and tools getting ready -- the head says Starting with the run's latest words, and the journal its log so far; the view's … menu opens the loop's Overview, Results or Live in your browser. Stop and Note are in the view's title bar while it runs, Stop now in its … menu; they work from the web too.

docs.title: Chat
docs.text:
The loop's Chat is a Flux tab in VS Code's agent panel, beside Claude Code or Codex. Chat about this loop in the Flux view's title bar opens it (the panel too, when it is closed); Ask Flux about this… among a box's or a step's buttons opens it on a new conversation about that box -- after a failed run, with how it failed. Ask, and the answer comes as on the web: the same agents, the same conversations (Open on the web in the tab's title bar), claude is looking · 23 s · 12 commands with Stop while it works.

When the agent proposes a change to problem.yaml, its settings or a document under library/, its card has Show diff -- VS Code's own diff of your file and the proposal, with Accept and Reject in its title bar -- and Accept, which writes the change in your folder (your other edits and undo kept), then tells the server: the web shows it Done · applied on your machine. A proposal made on a text your file no longer has (you edited it since) is refused with problem.yaml changed since this was proposed: nothing written -- ask for it again. Other proposals -- a note, an idea, a design note -- are made by the server, as on the web. New chat and Earlier chats are in the tab's title bar.

A loop living on your machine is answered here on your machine, its only place: the agents your problem.yaml defines (agents:), the agents installed here, and FluxAgent (its model is the server's). The agent works in your folder, as your loop's own agents do: your files as they are now, your .venv, your logins. Who answers lists them, with Default (the first) chosen until you pick one. Beside Think, Effort offers the agent's kind's levels (Default: its own). The answer says where it ran: codeagent · 1 min 12 s · here on fern. A reply asks the same agent. While your machine is offline (VS Code closed, the laptop asleep), or online with the loop's folder not open in any window, a question is refused at once -- wordline lives on fern, which is offline … or … which is online, but the loop's folder is not open in VS Code there; nothing waits to run later. A machine lost while it answers ends that answer, said in the conversation.

While a loop lives on your machine:

  • the web shows it on your machine, as any loop running on another machine;
  • its files are changed in VS Code: the web's file edits say so. What the web and the agents read follows your folder as you save -- a hand edit, a form, an accepted proposal, a file added or removed -- not only when a run ends (never what the runs write: out/, runs/, workbench/);
  • a run goes on when your machine loses the server, and catches up once it is back;
  • a Start waits for your machine to be online with the loop's folder open there (the Overview says which: open in VS Code now, online, its folder not open in VS Code, not heard for 3 h). Settings › Name & ownership › Take back makes the loop the server's again (a run still on your machine is stopped and what it sends late is set aside).

docs.title: Tour
docs.text:
Flux is a shared server with accounts, used in the browser. Each user has loops; each loop is a document and its files, run sandboxed on the server. Create, check, start, stop, follow and read loops here. Install starts a server.

Try it first in the Preview app: create a loop step by step, then a tour of the app, or the tour alone.

docs.title: Loops
docs.text:
The first page lists your loops. Each row shows:

  • its state, and its design agent (who works its Design box; tinted while running);
  • its designs as "2 / 12 / 30": accepted this start / accepted / all (every design handed in); the tooltip says accepted of measured (accepted and rejected), failed and pending. The Overview's Acceptance rate is accepted ÷ measured;
  • the decision's main measurements (Settings › Measurements' Main, else the first objective), green or red against their limits;
  • Start, Stop and Restart as small icons at the row's end.

Search, filter by state, sort by activity, name or decision. Shared with me lists loops shared with you or your group, with your rights ("ask · edit · run"). Archived loops are under Archived (Archive).

Project tabs: when you see a group's project, tabs above the search filter by project: All, one per project, In no project, each with a count. Under All, a Project column names each loop's first project and "+N" others (Groups). The chosen tab is remembered in this browser.

docs.title: New loop
docs.text: Way What it does Configurator A form in six steps (Create a loop in the Preview walks through it) Create or upload An empty loop, or one from a folder, files, a .zip, or a pasted document (Paste YAML) Direct edit Write the YAML yourself Agent An agent writes it from your prompt and files (Write a loop with an agent) Clone A copy of a loop's problem, without its runs

docs.title: A loop's page
docs.text:
The header has Start (▶) at rest, Stop (■) and Restart (↻) while running.

Tab What it shows Overview State, decision and objectives, best designs, best-so-far chart, notes, the agent's questions Live The run now and every pass, as a graph or timeline (Live) Results Every design measured, charts, ideas, library (Results) Agents Every model and agent turn, newest first: where (pass, box, try), outcome, prompt, reply, tool calls, time, tokens; session info ("resumed (turn k of K)", "new session", "warm start", "shared first session") Files The loop's files and the agents' workbench (Files and settings) Settings Preferences, sharing, maintenance, the problem (Files and settings)

An agent writing or revising the problem shows a strip at the top of the Overview until the loop starts, the document changes, or six hours pass. Hide from Overview hides an ended strip. Its history: Settings › Problem › Agent.

A loop that lives in VS Code (VS Code) has a VS Code tag beside its name in the list, and VS Code · on its page; hover the tag to see when the machine was last heard. Its runs go to that machine, so Start waits while the machine is not heard. Its files are read-only here: what would change them (editing the document, Add, Import, Reset, Archive) is turned off, with the reason. Change them in VS Code, or Take back the loop in Settings › Name & ownership. Rename still works here, and VS Code follows it.

docs.title: Overview cards
docs.text:
• Decision: the decision and its pill (✓ accepted; ! closest when nothing meets every requirement; ✗ failed), "ties with #229", "last pass 17 min ago". Hover the pill for the rule ("Decided by: smallest area_um2 at fmax_mhz >= 1000") and stage. Below: a tile per main measurement with its change from the reference, then Best 3.
    • The reference: the latest baseline at its stage, else the accepted designs' P10 (minimized) or P90 (maximized). Every page compares with the same reference.
  • Best: a chart per main measurement, titled "best cycles (-12.9%)" (or "best cycles 6189" without a baseline).
  • Starred designs (add it yourself): a tile per starred design, latest first.
  • Note to the loop and Agent asks: below.
  • Small cards (top row): State, Designs measured, Passes, Last improvement, Working now by default; up to 10.
Small card Shows Passes The loop's passes over every start, as its record counts them; while it runs, this start's too Last improvement When the best design last improved ("42 min ago"), which design, which pass, passes since Pass speed Median wall time of the last 20 passes, most at once, passes per hour Working now Agents and models at work, designs per box ("11 design · 3 check · 2 measure"); "idle" at rest Idea queue Ideas queued, evaluated, and proposed but neither Uptime How long this start has run; starts today One metric One metric's best accepted value and change from the baseline ("−12.9%"); the metric you type in the layout editor, else the first objective Stage funnel Designs made → passed checks → measured on the last stage

Customize cards in Account › Profile › Customize (Overview layout); Defaults restores them. Hidden cards cost nothing to load.

docs.title: Start, stop, restart
docs.text:
Start asks how many passes (one design each) or Until stopped.

  • A trunk asks for designs and says what runs ("trunk: 2 agents (claude (opus), codex), 3 evaluated at once, 5 handed in at most, pipelined").
  • A folder with several problems asks which; one that does not load is shown with why and a Direct edit link.
  • It checks the document first when inputs changed (as Settings › Problem › Check); on failure the button reads Start anyway.
  • A start resumes from the record. Started from the Loops list, you stay on the list (Started, with Open).
  • A failed loop shows Start again. While an agent writes the problem, Start waits.

Stop and Restart act after the current pass. The asked button turns red with an hourglass, an amber pill shows "Stops after pass 4" or "Restarts after pass 4", and the loop stays running until then. Press the other to switch. Press the same one again (it turns solid red) to act now: it asks, then abandons the pass.

docs.title: A loop's Chat
docs.text:
Chat, on every tab of a loop, opens a panel with one conversation about the loop.

  • The bar: the conversation's name (opens the list, with + New chat and Delete), Open in Chat (opens it in the top bar's Chat), Close.
  • Ask puts a question (why it stalls, which design is best, what to try) to an agent or FluxAgent. It reads the loop and changes nothing.
  • Thinking & commands under an answer shows how it was made.
  • Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line.
  • A dot on Chat means the loop's agent is asking you something.
  • The loop's chats share a Chat workbench (editors only), separate from the loop's own workbench/ (A loop's Chat workbench).
  • Old #/app/NAME/ask and #/app/NAME/talk links open it; #/app/NAME/chat/ID opens one conversation.

Note to the loop (Overview card): a note sent while the loop runs reaches its agents at the next step (a trunk: each agent's next turn), and every step while it stands.

  • Enter sends. A loop at rest has no box.
  • Notes are listed newest first. A filled dot: read ("Read at pass 14"); a ring: waiting.
  • The latest three show; N more shows up to twenty.
  • Editors remove a note with its bin. An unread note then never arrives; a read one leaves the agents' next messages.

Agent asks (Overview card): the agent's question with its choices, You decide and a free answer; your answer goes as a note. Answered questions are listed below. Hidden when there is nothing.

The question's line above the tabs, and the bell, lead there. With the card hidden, Answer opens a dialog.

Chat in the top bar is the same, bound to no loop (Chat); its rail lists your loops' conversations (Loop chats).

docs.title: Everywhere
docs.text:
• Top bar: Chat · Loops · Groups · Admin (admins). New loop is at the end of the Loops list's search bar.
  • Theme: system, light or dark; remembered in this browser.
  • Your name opens Account. While an admin views as a user, it shows that user's name.
  • Bell: a run ends or fails, an agent asks, a loop is shared with you.
  • Browser tab: names what is open ("cpu_tune — Loop", "CPU block diagram — Chat"). Its icon's dot: pink something waits for you, red failed, blue running or answering.
  • Live updates: pages refresh only what changed, keeping your scroll and selection. An editor you are typing in is never replaced: Changed on the server offers Reload. A background tab pauses and catches up when you return.
  • Long lists load more as you scroll ("N of M").
  • Raw and Fullscreen on files, logs, results and agent turns.
  • Addresses name the view: #/app/NAME/live/timeline, #/app/NAME/settings/problem?step=graph.
  • Phone: account items move to the menu button; lists and tabs stack.

The Preview app runs these pages on sample data.

docs.title: Server and admin
docs.text: Run a Flux server, manage accounts, groups and projects, and set the server's agents, sandbox, chat and maintenance.

docs.title: The server
docs.text:
Installing and starting one: Install; for a team, the system service. Everything else is on these pages.

  • Data: the database, secret.key (encrypts keys and secrets) and every loop. Back up the database and secret.key together (Admin › Server › Maintenance), loop folders separately. Never copy the database alone while the server runs (Backups and restore).
  • Limits: a loop holds up to 100,000 files and 8 GB; one upload 900 files and 256 MB. No cap on a user's loops at once: a run is a machine's (Machines).
  • Restarts: running loops are found again; their containers keep running meanwhile.
  • TLS proxy: for others to reach the server, put one in front; it must not buffer the live connection (nginx: the server sends X-Accel-Buffering: no).
  • Before login, only the sign-in page is served. Logging in or out in one tab updates the others.
  • After an update, open pages load the new version once.

docs.title: Agents' Tests
docs.text:
A start waits until each agent its problem names passed its Test for the loop's owner, with the current configuration ("Codex not set up for cedric yet (its configuration changed since its Test)"). A new agent version needs new Tests.

  • Each user tests their own in Account › Agents: run in their home with their settings; no credential is seen.
  • Admin › Server › Maintenance › Test agents runs them for every user on a schedule (or Run now): each user's set-up agents ("set up": logged in, own key, endpoint, model or variable, or tested before), in their loops' contexts. Disabled users are skipped.
  • A Test times out after 420 s. A failure is listed in Admin › Loops › Failures.
  • Audited as the user's "agent test". Not counted in usage.

docs.title: Accounts
docs.text:
Admin › People › Users makes an account: a name, a password (empty: an invitation link to send the user) and a group, then Add. Links work once, for a week; there is no mail.

Admin › People › Users: a row per user with Admin, Create, Run, Internals, Active (off disables the account), groups (×, +), Last active, Show usage, and ⋯: View as (read-only), a reset or invitation link, Rename, Delete.

Permission Gives Admin Administers the server and every loop. Implies Create, Run, Internals. You cannot clear your own Create loops Makes loops Run loops and agents Runs loops, Ask and agents Internals ("See how Flux works") Lets a person see how the loop works inside. Without it, turns show only replies and counts (Live); a Chat proposal is accepted by someone who has it. No group or project role gives it; audited
  • A new password logs the user out everywhere (from a link or an admin). Changed on their own Account, it keeps the current session.
  • Settings layer field by field: the server's, then each group's (by group name; later wins), then the user's. An empty field inherits. Keys and models never pair with a lower layer's endpoint; token prices are the endpoint's layer's (A group's agents).
  • Groups: a user is in none, one or several. Admin › People › Groups lists each group with members, Open projects level (Asker by default), Rename and Delete. Unrolled: the member grid (Level, a box per word, ×; All members; People adds as Member). The same grid serves projects and loop Sharing.
  • Group membership gives nothing on any loop (the words).
  • A loop is reached only by a share or by a project it is linked into. Your rights are your row, your groups' rows and your projects', together. Ask and Run also need Run loops and agents.
  • Archive, reset, delete, rename and transfer belong to the owner and admins.

docs.title: The words
docs.text:
One vocabulary everywhere.

  • Loop words: view, ask, edit, run (on a shared loop or a project's loops); share (a loop's own: give the loop to others, at most what you hold).
  • Place words: link (link your loops into a project), curate (review knowledge, keep the library), manage (members, levels, access, title; rename, archive, delete), create (groups only: make projects; the maker is Lead).
Place Words Loop share view · ask · edit · run · share Group membership curate · manage · create Project level view · ask · edit · run · link · curate · manage Global project level curate · manage

Levels (a mix is Custom):

Level Words Loop Project Group Global project Member none -- yes yes yes Viewer view yes yes -- -- Asker view · ask yes yes -- -- Contributor view · ask · edit · run · link yes (no link) yes -- -- Maintainer Contributor and curate, create (on a loop: view · ask · edit · run · share) yes yes curate · create curate Lead every word -- yes curate · manage · create curate · manage
  • A loop's levels stop at Maintainer; Owner is shown, never given.
  • Words acting on a loop imply view.
  • Managers give levels up to their own; admins any.
  • Why some boxes are missing: linking needs share on the loop and link on the project; a loop is not curated; managing a loop is the owner's; groups never carry loop words or share; projects do not nest; a global project's visibility gives view and it gives no loop words.

What a group gives on its projects' loops: only the project's group access: invite (default; nothing, hidden), view, or open (the project's open level, Asker by default). Its curate, manage and create reach every project of the group.

Global projects are public (everyone sees them) or private (members and admins only). Members hold only curate or manage. Only admins and managers see others' loops in one. Who links: everyone or admins (a private one: members only).

docs.title: Renames
docs.text:
• User (admins: ⋯ › Rename): everything moves (folder, caches, settings, shares, runs, schedules, chats, usage). Refused while anything of theirs runs. No redirects: people their loops are shared with, and the user, are told the new link. Sessions stay. One "rename user" audit entry.
  • Group (pencil in Admin › People › Groups): members, permissions and shares stay; members are told. Names ignore case; _ reserved, / refused. Refused while a linked loop runs.

docs.title: Deletes
docs.text:
• Active off disables a user: logged out, everything kept.
  • ⋯ › Delete (admins): the dialog lists their loops, sole-managed projects, shares and groups, and asks whether their loops are transferred to a user (a clashing name becomes <loop>-<user>) or deleted. Everything else of theirs goes; the audit and history stay. Refused while anything of theirs runs, for yourself, and for the last admin. Type their name to confirm.
  • Groups › Delete: refused while it has projects (archived too; listed with links). It lists members, shared loops, its agents and settings (loops naming its agents will not start) and its machines (revoked). Type its name. Members keep their accounts and loops.

docs.title: A group's agents
docs.text:
A group's Agents tab (#/groups/<id>/agents, admins and managers) is the layer between the server's settings and each member's.

  • FluxAgent and a tab per agent: endpoint, model, key, seconds per turn, prices (turns at once stay the server's, except for the group's own agents). A set field shows "over server"; an empty one "from server"; ↺ resets. Keys are encrypted and shown only as "set".
  • Per agent: variables, instructions (after the server's, before each member's), thinking by default, and Test (counts for each member who inherits exactly that configuration).
  • All agents: variables for every agent.
  • + Add: a group's own agent (name, Program -- one of the server's, OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex --, label, extra arguments). Documents name it <group>/<name> (group name lower-cased, other characters _: Team A/foo is team_a/foo), or by name alone if unambiguous (by: foo is refused if two groups have one). It shows program not found until its program is found here.
  • Audited (group settings, group agent added, changed, removed), never values. Members see the result in Account › Agents.
  • A renamed group's agents become <new>/<name>; <old>/<name> still works until reused.
  • A member removed from a group loses its layer from their next run.

docs.title: A group's schedule
docs.text:
The Schedule card schedules the group's own agents' turns at once, as Scheduled changes do (+ Schedule, Run now, Edit, Turn off/Turn on, Delete). Never above the admin's limits:

  • the stricter of the group's and the admin's value applies;
  • an agent on the same endpoint as a server agent shares its slots;
  • the server's pause still applies.

The card says when the admin's limit is stricter ("The admin's limit is stricter: at most 2 at once (shared with OpenCode on box.example:8080)"). Audited (group schedule). Admin › Maintenance › Schedule lists them read-only.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text:
A project belongs to one group (<group>/<name>) or is global (_/<name>, shown "global / …"). Names: letters, digits, -, _, unique per group regardless of case. See Groups and a project's page.

A group's project is made on the group's page (New project: name, title, group access), a global one by admins (New global project in Admin › People › Projects). Members, levels, access, rename, archive and delete are on the project's page (Groups).

  • Levels: the words on a project. The maker is Lead. A Member sees the project and its members only.
  • Group access: invite (default; hidden), view, open (the open level).
  • Rights only add up: group access, group membership's curate/manage, project level, a global project's visibility.
  • A project's contents (files, knowledge, chats) are its own members' and admins' only (Groups).
  • Members with create make a group's projects; only admins make global ones.
  • Archiving hides and freezes a project. Everything is audited.

Admin › People › Projects lists every project: title, address, group, loops, members, library use ("6 B of 2 KB", over when above). Per global project: Visibility, Who links loops. Row tools: open, rename, archive/unarchive, delete. New global project is below.

Library limits: Library limit for every project (GB), or a row's Limit; empty inherits (finally a loop's 8 GB). Audited ("library limit"). An over-limit library cannot grow.

docs.title: Loops in projects
docs.text:
A loop is in none, one or several projects, in an order its owner sets. Only its owner (or an admin) links it: into a group's project where they hold link, or a global one per its join rule. Archived projects take none.

  • In a group's project, members get their loop words on it; the group's members what its access gives. Never takes rights away. Ask and run still need Run loops and agents.
  • A global project gives no rights; users see only their own loops there.
  • Each link has learning (the collector): on by default in a group's project; in a global one off until an admin or manager turns it on.
  • Renamed or transferred loops keep their projects; a deleted project unlinks its loops and tells the owners.

The owner sets them in the loop's Settings › Preferences › Projects (Files and settings): Add to a project…, the order, Learns, ✕. A project's page lists its loops.

docs.title: Your account
docs.text:
Account has four tabs (#/account/agents; #/account opens Profile):

  • Profile: your groups, usage, password (asks the current one; logs out other sessions), desktop notifications, Overview layout.
  • Agents: a tab per agent: login, Test, model, variables, your allowed hosts, your own instructions; All agents for shared variables. Fields show "from server", "from group", or "over group" with ↺. Your groups' own agents have tabs too.
  • Machines: your machines (Add my machine) and the others your loops may use (Machines).
  • Shared links: every link you made (Share), with opens, Copy, Revoke; stopped when you lost the right.

An agent is used only once its Test passed for whoever starts the loop. Tests run at once, outside any limit (Agents' Tests). Logins run in the sandbox in a small terminal; Claude Code's token is stored encrypted. Without its own settings an agent uses its own configuration (Models and agents).

docs.title: Admin
docs.text:
Five tabs; each opens on the sub-tab last used in this browser. Old addresses (#/admin/users, #/admin/insights) still work.

Tab Sub-tab What it holds Loops All loops Every user's loops; pause new starts; stop or restart all after their pass Failures Failed starts and agent Tests People Users Users and permissions, invitations, View as Groups Every group and its members Projects Every project Runtime Agents FluxAgent and each agent: program, login, model, key, seconds per turn, token prices, turns at once per endpoint, allowed hosts, enabled, offered for Ask, thinking by default, instructions; + Add agent Machines Every machine; every loop runs on one, never on the server Sandbox Limits, network, PATH directories mounted, what every user's home starts with Chat What users may use in Chat (Chat) Activity Resources CPU, memory, disks over time; the tool pool (resource hints); sandbox containers; disk per loop Usage Usage and cost by user and agent; disk now Endpoints How each endpoint did; hosts the network refused Commands What the loops' agents ran (Commands) Audit The audit trail, newest first; filter by What, Who and search Server Version The running commit, updates, Update and Roll back (Version) Maintenance Scheduled tasks and setting changes
  • Keys are encrypted and never shown again. With nothing set, runs use each agent's own configuration on the server's machine.
  • Model of an agent without an endpoint: From the agent lists the agent's own models (as each user's login sees them); Default leaves it to the agent; with the box off, type any name.
  • Which model wins: a document's model:, then the loop's variable, then Account › Agents, then Admin › Runtime › Agents.
  • An agent's panel shows: installed (path on hover) or missing ("claude is not on the runs' PATH"), version, document name; Connection and Verification pills with Test; Program, Name shown; Enabled, Offered for Ask, Thinks by default and efforts; under Fine-tune: Interface, login command, extra arguments, login files, home files, hosts.
  • Interface: how the program is driven -- Claude Code's, Codex's or OpenCode's command line. Default is what the program says to --help (the words beside the menu say which); a pick is an override. An added agent needs only a name and a Program; one whose --help names no known interface says interface not told (hover for why) and is offered to no one until Interface is set. An agent is shown everywhere by its own name and its program's version, never by the interface's name.
  • Users are offered only agents whose program is found; a document naming another shows (not available).
  • An added agent runs its own Program, else its interface's own.

docs.title: Allowed hosts
docs.text: Allowed hosts (each agent's settings, Admin › Agents and Account › Agents): hosts a run of the agent on a full machine lent its login may reach beside its endpoint's -- an allowlist as typed (Allowlists); the server's, a group's and the user's own add up, so Account › Agents shows only your own (never "from server"). Such a run's network is always an allowlist: the agent's own endpoint (or, with none and its kind's program, its kind's service), these hosts, the document's hosts: for the agent (agent options), the sandbox allowlist below, the loop's extra hosts and the Flux server. Runs on this server keep the sandbox's network setting.

docs.title: Enabled
docs.text:
Untick Enabled to switch an agent off. It is offered nowhere (a document naming it shows (disabled by an admin)), and starts, chats, asks and Tests naming it are refused: claude is disabled on this server by an admin. Running loops keep it until they stop. Audited (agent disabled, agent enabled).

Other agents of the same interface are unaffected: an added aide driven as Claude Code still runs its own Program, else the built-in's. Use Enabled, not a bogus Program, to disable.

docs.title: Thinking by default
docs.text:
Each agent's panel sets whether it Thinks by default (where a loop's box does not say: Thinking; and how Chat's Think starts: Chat), with its effort when thinking and when not (Default leaves it to the agent). FluxAgent's efforts: low, medium, high, max; its Default is high thinking, medium not (said in the menu's tooltip).

Thinks by default Effort when thinking when not Each agent on its own its kind's lowest (low, or minimal) FluxAgent off built in (high) built in (medium)

Precedence: a chat's Think, then the loop's box, then this default. Audited (thinking by default); applies to runs started afterwards.

Structured answers (FluxAgent, on by default): asks the model for answers in a fixed shape; a design answer not in that shape is asked for once more, never read from the text. Turn it off for a model server that cannot: designs are then read from the reply's text, and the run's log says so.

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text: Instructions: text given to the agent with every task (loops, Chat, New loop › Agent, its Test). Not FluxAgent. OpenCode ships with a default (Default restores it). At most 4,000 characters; audited (agent instructions). Groups and users add their own after the server's (Account › Agents); a loop's turns use its owner's.

docs.title: Resources
docs.text:
• Over time: CPU, memory, disks (30 days), beside every loop's tokens per second; Runs CPU and Runs memory: what the runs use, measured over each run's processes whatever they run in (a sandboxed step's container, a plain process on a machine without one); Running: loops and steps. Containers are a series of these only where the range shown had any.
  • Sandbox containers: CPU, memory, processes. Whose: a loop's (Stop after its pass), Chat · user (Stop), Login · user, Agent test · user. left behind containers have Kill (the clean-up removes them too).
  • Compiler caches: each user's ccache size.
  • Disk per loop: each loop's inputs, record, log, workbench, cache and scratch. A loop not yet measured says measuring… until its folder is walked (in the background). A loop living on a VS Code machine is tagged: its sizes are the server's copy.
  • Machine picker: this server or a joined machine, the same charts (its CPU, load, memory, disks, its runs; a storage machine's bytes served). Figures arrive with each heartbeat (~15 s), kept 30 days.
  • Orphan caches: sandbox caches no loop owns (a deleted loop's, or not the web's). Each says whether Clean disk removes it next (goes at the next clean) or why not (in use, used in the last 14 days). Clean now runs that part; Delete removes one. A cache owned by another account says how to remove it on the server's machine.

docs.title: The memory guard
docs.text:
When the machine runs short of memory (RAM above Stop above, 95%, with swap over the Swap mark, 80%, or filling), the server stops the loop using the most memory, then the next, until RAM is under Until under (90%). A chat sandbox can be stopped too.

  • The loop ends failed; earlier passes are kept. Why it stopped says e.g. Stopped to free memory: the machine was at 96% (30.7 GB of 32.0 GB); this loop used 11.4 GB, the most of any.
  • Logged, audited (memory guard), and the owner is notified. It is not restarted.
  • The Server card shows memory and swap use and the last stop. Edit sets on/off and the marks (50% to 99%); audited (memory guard settings).

docs.title: The sandbox scratch cap
docs.text:
A loop's sandbox scratch (pass working files) is capped by its Scratch /tmp size: the loop's own (Settings › Advanced), else the server's default (Admin › Runtime › Sandbox › Limits), held to the maximum. None set: no cap.

Clean disk trims each scratch every five minutes, oldest first; never recent files, a running loop's current work, or the baseline's and decision's files. Reported in the loop's log, Maintenance history and Disk per loop (trimmed 4.2 GiB today). Trimmed files show no longer kept.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Admin › Activity › Commands summarises what the loops' agents ran over 1, 7 or 30 days (UTC), per loop, agent and mode: commands and flags that do not exist, each flux command's uses and failures, shell programs and tools, commands repeated across turns, turns and failures. No output beyond known error lines. Export saves JSON. Up to a minute behind.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
Task What it does Its setting Clean disk Frees disk: leftover containers, old scratch and pass folders (a run's newest stays), sandbox caches unused for two weeks; warns of low disk; optionally Flux's temporary folder older than (days), 3; Flux's temporary folder too Condense history Shortens big logs, journals and old agent transcripts, keeping their recent part. Never results, ideas or decisions older than (days), 14 Compact and check Compacts and checks the database and every record; loads each stopped loop's document; with backups kept over 0, saves the database and secret.key to backups/ backups kept, 0 (no backup) Prune server tables Expired sessions and invitations; old login failures, notifications, refused-host log; old audit lines older than (days), 30; audit (days), 365 (0: all kept) Prune run history Keeps each loop's latest starts in the run list keep, 200 Test agents Off by default: the agents' Tests, below none Clean leftovers Off by default: what updates leave behind, below. Never a record none
  • Default schedules: Clean disk every minute; Compact and check and Clean leftovers weekly; the others daily. Every run is audited.
  • Running loops are touched only where the table says; archived loops only by checks and compaction.
  • Record edits are the loop's own (Settings › Record, never scheduled): Prune stale records, Prune empty starts, Prune failed designs (pick a stage, or Any stage; e.g. Deletes 143 failed designs (stage gate) in bob/x: their rows, their designs' text and the pass files only they have ... Cannot be undone.), Invalidate all, Re-Evaluate (Results).
  • Test agents: each user's set-up agents, in their loops' contexts, and the server's shared configurations as the first admin (Agents' Tests). Two at once; outside limits; audited "(by maintenance)". One failure fails the run; a user whose Test newly fails is told.
  • Clean leftovers (after an update, or weekly), on every loop at rest or one:
Left behind By Removed when A copy of a loop's document an earlier Flux, when it updated the document the document is there and loads What the server keeps to start sooner after a restart the server an earlier version made it, or it was never finished

It never removes a loop's record or a copy of one: those are listed as kept for you to delete. It skips running loops. Each removal is audited. Old prepared environments are removed by updates themselves.

Tabs: Tasks (running, queued, failed, done, off), Schedule (scheduled changes), History (every run, the last 1000; chips Failed, Schedule, Run now).

  • Each task has Run now and Edit. One task runs at a time; others queue (queued · 2nd, Cancel). A restart drops the queue.
  • Run now asks first when it deletes or rewrites data (Deletes pass folders older than 3 days in 12 loops (3 running) ... Cannot be undone.), and says nothing when there is nothing to do. Also from Edit › One loop › Run and a loop's own Settings.
  • On one loop: Clean disk trims scratch, removes old pass folders and its sandbox cache; Condense history condenses its log, journal and transcript; Compact and check compacts, checks and loads its document.
  • Schedules: every N minutes, hours or days; daily at a time on picked days; or cron. A time already past waits for the next day.

docs.title: Backups and restore
docs.text:
Back up server database saves the database and secret.key to backups/server-<time>/ while the server runs.

To restore:

  1. Stop the server.
  2. Move flux-web.db and any flux-web.db-wal and flux-web.db-shm aside (keep them).
  3. Put the backup's flux-web.db and secret.key in the data folder.

  4. Start the server.

  5. Never copy a database in while the server runs.

  6. A start that finds mismatched files is refused, naming them; nothing is deleted. Copy all three together before moving any: the -wal holds committed changes.

docs.title: Scheduled changes
docs.text:
+ Schedule: pick a kind, its fields, then when.

Kind What it does Turns at once Sets an agent endpoint's turns at once or FluxAgent's requests at once (whole number; 0 no limit). Group agents are scheduled by the group (A group's schedule) Pause starts Pauses new starts with a reason (up to 200 characters), or resumes. Running loops go on; starts and restarts are refused with the reason Stop loops Stops running loops after their pass: all, one user's, or one. Now stops at once Start a loop Starts one loop as its owner, with its last start's options, for 1–1000 passes or until stopped. Refused (a failed run) if gone, archived, owner disabled, starts paused, or already running
  • When: daily at a time on picked days, or Advanced: cron expression (*/15 9-17 * * 1-5: every 15 minutes, 09:00-17:59, weekdays). Server time zone, shown.
  • Each row: schedule, next and last run, result, Run now, Edit, Turn off/Turn on, Delete.
  • Changes apply at every loop's next turn. Lowering a limit stops no running turn.
  • A missed stop or start is not done later. Settings (pause, limits) take their latest past value when the server starts.
  • Audited, e.g. scheduled: Claude Code turns at once → 4 (was 1).

Example: people by day, loops by night:

Change When Claude Code turns at once → 1 daily at 08:00, Mon–Fri Claude Code turns at once → 4 daily at 20:00, every day

A nightly run: Start a loop at 20:00 until stopped; Pause starts at 20:05 (nightly runs); Stop loops at 07:00 after their pass; Pause starts → Resume starts at 07:30.

docs.title: Sandbox
docs.text: Every run is sandboxed unless a loop's Settings › Preferences › Advanced (admins) says otherwise. Network: open, or an allowlist; HTTP(S) goes through the proxy; raw TCP/UDP is per loop (Sandbox).

docs.title: Allowlists
docs.text:
Every allowlist (sandbox, Chat, a loop's extra hosts, an agent's hosts):

Entry Allows dl.acm.org that host only *.acm.org or .acm.org acm.org and every subdomain (dl.acm.org, www.acm.org, a.b.acm.org) 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.1.20, ::1 the addresses in the range, or that address localhost this machine (127.0.0.1, ::1)
  • Separate by new lines, commas, semicolons or spaces; # comments.
  • Case, a trailing dot and a port are ignored (DL.ACM.org.:443 is dl.acm.org); a pasted URL keeps its host.
  • * alone is refused: choose open.
  • The page shows how it reads (Understood as: acm.org and its subdomains · arxiv.org only).
  • A redirect to another domain is refused by that host. Recently blocked lists refused hosts; click to add. The agent sees: flux sandbox: refused www.acm.org (not on the network allowlist -- add www.acm.org or *.acm.org). The refusals file names the agent whose turn asked (agent) when the request came from an agent's turn.

Limits apply to every sandbox (runs, checks, chats, the author, Tests, logins). For CPUs, memory, processes and scratch /tmp:

  • Default: when the loop sets none.
  • Maximum: higher asks are clamped (memory 8 GB clamped to 1 GB by the server).
  • Empty: no limit (processes: 4096).

CPUs: e.g. 2 or 0.5, up to the machine's count. Memory and scratch in GB (128, 0.5), memory up to the machine's RAM. Scratch also caps disk use (the sandbox scratch cap). Audited (sandbox limits); new sandboxes only. Read-only on a server started without the sandbox.

docs.title: Proxy
docs.text:
The proxy for runs, agents, Chat, logins, the author, and Flux's model calls, sandboxed or not.

  • From the host (default): the server's environment, /etc/environment, /etc/environment.d/*.conf, ~/.config/environment.d/*.conf, then the login shell's exports. Shown as e.g. From /etc/environment: HTTP http://proxy:3128 · not for .corp.example.org.
  • Set here: HTTP and HTTPS proxies (http://host:port, optionally user:password@) and a not through it list (hosts, .domain, *.domain, IPs, CIDRs). Credentials are encrypted and shown as http://***@proxy:3128.
  • Sandboxes get HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY (localhost always added).
  • In effect shows the result. Audited (sandbox proxy); applies to what starts afterwards.

docs.title: Chat
docs.text:
Admin › Runtime › Chat sets what users may use in Chat; users switch allowed features per chat.

Feature Allowed Default Chat tab The user has Chat in the top bar. Off, every other feature is off too. on Network beyond the base allowlist A chat may also reach the hosts listed under Network beyond the base (These hosts), or any host when it is Open. off Workbench A chat may read and write the user's workbench. on Loop access A chat may read the user's loops, their own and those shared with them, read-only. on
  • Everyone is the server's value; Overrides per group and user (default, on, off). User beats group beats server; among groups, off wins. Add user adds a row.
  • Chats always have the sandbox's base allowlist (Sandbox). With nothing listed and not Open, the network feature stays off.
  • A disabled feature is greyed with why (turned off by the admin on this server, for the group …, for you).
  • Applies from each chat's next message. Audited (chat permissions, chat created, chat deleted).

FluxAgent on the web (web tools; only with the chat's Network on; never private addresses):

Setting Default MB each 50 1 to 500. A larger download is refused. Seconds a fetch 60 5 to 300. Ports beyond 80 and 443 none For example 8080. Other ports are refused. Web search None SearXNG (its address, for example https://searx.example.org), or Brave Search (its subscription token).
  • Paper search needs export.arxiv.org and api.openalex.org allowed.
  • The search provider is reached as set, regardless of the host list.
  • The Brave key is encrypted; replace or Clear it. Fetches are audited (chat web).

Other limits:

Setting Default Range Minutes per coding-agent answer 8 1 to 60 Tool calls per coding-agent answer 40 5 to 400 Diagram tries (Chat) 5 0 to 10 Attached MB each (Attached files) 50 1 to 2048 Attached Files a message 10 1 to 50 Sandbox kept idle (minutes; 0: one sandbox per answer) 30 0 to 240
  • An answer stopped at a limit keeps what was written; with nothing written it fails, naming the limit.
  • How Think starts: thinking by default.
  • Answers run sandboxed under the server's limits with the user's agent settings.
