A topic with entries cannot be removed.</li> </ul> <h2 id="global">Global<a class="headerlink" href="#global" title="Permanent link">¶</a></h2> <p><strong>Global</strong> lists public global projects and private ones you belong to.</p> <ul> <li>Only admins create them: <strong>New global project</strong> in <strong>Admin › People › Projects</strong> (public, or private).</li> <li>Anyone may link a loop into a public one; a private one's members into it.</li> <li>Linking gives nobody rights on the loop; you see only your own loops in it.</li> <li>Learning is off until an admin or manager turns it on.</li> </ul> <h2 id="in-no-group">In no group<a class="headerlink" href="#in-no-group" title="Permanent link">¶</a></h2> <p>You see an explanation, <strong>Global</strong>, and your loops under <strong>Loops</strong>.</p> <h2 id="admins">Admins<a class="headerlink" href="#admins" title="Permanent link">¶</a></h2> <p>An admin's <strong>▾</strong> lists every group ("not a member" where so). Admins set any level, add and remove members, make projects, and see every group's <strong>Agents</strong> and <strong>Machines</strong> tabs. <strong>Every group in Admin › People › Groups</strong> opens the admin page.</p>

docs.title: Live
docs.text: A loop's Live tab shows its run task by task as it happens, and replays earlier starts. Two views: Graph (default) and Timeline (live/timeline). Old live/tree and live/log addresses open the Graph; the start's log is in Files, and on the Overview's Log when a run stopped on an error.

docs.title: The toolbar
docs.text:
• Start: which start to show: the running one or an older one (latest 50; Earlier for more).
  • Follow: keep the latest work in view. Scrolling, zooming or selecting stops it; press again to resume.
  • The head: Tasks, the start's tasks and their counts (done, failed, retried). The loop's passes are the Overview's Passes, counted from its record.
  • With pipelining off and three passes or more, a hint may say "Pipelining could make passes about 24% shorter: Settings › Problem › Extra › Pipelining." (shown at 10% or more).

docs.title: Graph
docs.text:
One pass as the loop's boxes: Search, Design, Check, Measure, Choose, and any critic.

  • Each box says its setting, ✓ or ✗, and ×N when it ran again. Skipped boxes are dashed.
  • A design of several tries has a bar per try: ✓, ! (not built) or ✗.
  • Pass chain above: a bubble per pass, coloured by outcome (Pass 4 shown). Click one to draw it. … expands every pass; Less folds them.
  • Ideas: a pass testing a queued idea skips search; Search says queued idea, and the inspector links to Results › Ideas. A design that takes a suggested idea says suggested idea.
  • Check and Measure have a bar per step (check or stage), not per run. The tooltip sums its runs (check unit: 9 of 11 passed, 1 failed, 1 running); a click opens the latest. A stage not reached yet is grey (measurement perf: waiting), hollow once the pass is over (not reached).
  • Design opens the agent's draft and conversation. Its Rationale lists the key changes and why.
  • Agents go by the names the document gives them (codeagent, defined under agents:); the tooltip adds the kind it runs as (codeagent (Claude Code)). A Search the document gives an agent says who picks, as VS Code's graph does (codeagent · explore). Its agent picks from the second pass on: a first draft follows the search policy, and Search says so.
  • Many designs at once (a re-check, several per pass): one row per design, a dot per check or stage (✓ #214 ●●●●, ✓ #246 ●● 24m 07s). Dots: green done, red failed, blue running, grey waiting, hollow never reached. The latest five show ("34 earlier designs" folded). Click a row for its checks or stages, then each for its command, exit and output.
  • A stage that exits non-zero is a failed measurement (red dot, ✗).
  • Standing design measured again: after a pass, the standing design is measured on the same stage to compare fairly. If it had to be re-measured, its row has an amber tag: tools changed, inputs changed, command changed, readout changed, vars changed, last try failed or not cached, with details (yosys rebuilt, bench.py edited). Old numbers are kept.

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text:
The start over time in three rows. Long starts scroll sideways.

Row Shows Setup Each pass's Setup (grey: Setup steps), the start's steps (opening the record, a reused baseline, the re-check queue, closing the record), a Choose that ran without a tool slot, the background tasks, and a rest on an endpoint that stayed down (a faint dotted line). One line at every zoom: steps at once overlap, the shorter drawn on top Design A line per lane (a trunk's: a line per trunk). A pass stays on its lane: Search (yellow), then a bar per try (blue), then the design's tag (#42), all one box. A turn waiting for its endpoint is hatched where its work would be. With pipeline, a repair that waited for its lane is a dashed box on the same lane. A lane held by a re-check (R5.5) is a faint dotted line Tool A line per tool slot. A design's Check, each Measure stage and Choose in one box on the slot they held, the design's tag at the box's right end; dashed while running. Agent probes are hatched, outlined in pink. A step's wait for room on the machine is a hatched grey block inside its box
  • Hover a design anywhere to light all its parts.
  • One pass at a time: passes are alternating columns, numbered at the top.
  • A bar is work, not waiting. A step's wait is a hatched grey block where it waited: for room on this machine's pool (cores, memory) inside its box on the Tool row -- the box begins at the step's ask, and a design whose first step still waits is a box holding the block alone -- or, for a tool slot, on its design's own Design line. Hover it: "Check: waited 27s for room on this machine (needs 1 core, 4 GB; free 0 cores, 1 GB)", "Measure · screen: waited 1m 10s for a tool slot", "so far" while it waits. An agent's own probe (flux loop gate|measure) waiting is drawn the same, from the moment it asked. An ideas cleanup waiting for a turn between its requests is a faint dotted line on its line. A turn waiting for its endpoint (down or busy: no try spent, no slot held) is hatched on its line, its tooltip naming the endpoint, how long and the tries since it last answered; after 30 minutes the run rests, a dotted line on Setup until it answers (When an agent's endpoint fails).
  • Designs decide in the order their measurements end. A trunk design that waited for earlier ones keeps its tool slot, and a faint dotted line in its box before its Choose says so on hover: "waited 1m 10s to decide after #3898 (2 ahead)". A flow design waits only while another design's decision is being made, and keeps its slot the same way.
  • A pink strip along a bar's foot marks where an agent or FluxAgent worked.
  • A repaired design is one box with its tag (#4), whichever try passed. A re-check or a draft you Evaluate runs as an R unit, numbered after the pass before it: R5.5 in the chain, the rows and the tables. Its designs say re-checked or handed in, evaluated.
  • Stop now marks the steps it cut interrupted (amber), never failed. The next start first measures what was cut: a bar per design, catch-up of a stopped run.
  • The head says what runs: pass 3, or passes 5–8 while several run at once.
  • A row shows at most six lines ("+3" hidden). The unroll tool, or clicking "+3", shows all; this browser remembers.
  • Click a bar to open it; Tab and Enter step through bars. A Setup bar opens its whole Setup (a pass's, the start's, a bud's, or Background in a run from before Nov 18) as the Graph's box lists it, the clicked step picked; click a step there to open it alone. Other work drawn on the Setup row (a Choose, a Plan, a Search bud's turn) opens itself.
  • Zoom out, Zoom in, Fit to the window; Ctrl+wheel (or pinch) zooms at the pointer; double-click zooms to a bar. Zoom is kept per loop until the tab closes.
  • A Setup step under half a second is a note, not a bar. Per box: calls, average, longest, total, share of the wall clock.

docs.title: A trunk-mode loop
docs.text:
A trunk loop shows trunks and branches instead of passes.

Graph:

  • A Design box per agent (Design · claude · t1): state (writing, queue full, waiting, stopped), turn, time, designs handed in.
  • A bar per hand-in: box colour when measured, red failed Check, amber error, faint pending. The latest 10 show; +137 counts earlier ones.
  • Click the box for the agent's latest turn.
  • 3 running · 2 waiting of 6, then a chain: Setup (S), a chip per design (#42), running ones with a blue dot, waiting ones dashed. A Setup run again is a chip (S3).
  • Pick a chip to draw its branch (Check, Measure, Choose). Live opens on the latest running branch.
  • Run setup (beside Stop) runs Setup again, document unchanged; its ideas cleanup ignores the thresholds. Greyed while one runs; audited.
  • Buds run one at a time, Setup and Search in turn, the oldest due first.
  • A failed ideas cleanup shows a warning: "Ideas cleanup due (370 open, 310 new or changed) but not done", why, and when it retries. Fix the agent or pick another under Knowledge › Ideas.
  • An ideas cleanup goes on, round after round, while it merges or marks ideas. A Search bud that comes due meanwhile runs between two rounds; the cleanup goes on after it.

Timeline: the same rows and tools.

  • Setup: start steps, then each bud: a Setup bud's steps a bar each (papers, workbench, ideas), a Search bud's Setup steps and one bar for its Search. An ideas cleanup is one bar however many rounds its agent takes (they are listed when you click it). Hover for the name (Decision, S3, Q2) and who answered; click for the bud's steps, the clicked one picked.
  • Design: a line per trunk, a bar per turn (one design), its tag at the end (#47). Each turn has its transcript (Design · t3 · turn 4 · #47).
  • Tool: each design's Check, Measure stages and decision in one box; a failed Check ends red. The start's re-check sits under a grey band, R · re-check. A draft you Evaluate while a flow's passes run has its box here too, beside theirs, tagged with its design.

Counts on a trunk's Live are the picked start's only.

docs.title: The inspector
docs.text:
Select a task to open it.

  • Tool task: command, folder, exit, time, output (live).
  • Agent task: reply, then the conversation (text, thinking, tool calls with inputs and outputs).
  • Model try: tools called, then the reply in parts (why, idea, code, diffs), tokens.
  • Raw and Fullscreen show everything.

Internals permission (Admin › People › Users): only people with it see prompts, thinking and each action. Everyone else (the owner included) sees status, final reply, the search direction without its reason, and a count line: 14 tool calls · 3 probes · 12m 30s. This applies to every agent. Your own stage and check commands stay visible.

A turn starts with a row of pills: agent, model, status, exit 0, 37 turns, tokens, cost, thinking on, Tool calls (12). Hover for the label (tokens: 2.0M in · 19.0k out). The Agents tab and Chat show the same pills.

  • A task shows its path: Pass 2 › Design › try 8, … › try 8 › call 6.
  • An improve says its starting stage (from the esl stage).
  • A failed or unbuilt try says why.
  • A box lists its runs; a box still to come shows its setting (YAML folded).
  • A pass shows what it measured last and whether it was kept, where its time went, and each box ("Design · 3 tries · 2 not built"). A box never reached says "not run".
  • A check's failures read "14 of 18 fail".

Choose names its pick and pool, and how long it waited for earlier designs to decide. Its box says the objectives, each with its way ("cycle ↓ · inst +3"); a tracked one has no arrow and is never a best.

  • A design a critic rejected is struck through with a critic tag; the reason is below. The tag, Open and Choose · critique · #N -- rejected open the critic's turn.
  • A dictionary metric shows one number: its objective's aggregate, else its _a, else the mean. Hover for entries.
  • Designs not in the pool are muted with why: "screen only", "cut on screen", "stale", "same design as #137", "rejected by the critic", "the baseline", a removed stage, or why not recorded.
  • If one beats the pick, a notice names it: "3 designs have a smaller jx_time than #131 and were not in the pool: #140 (377 ns) was measured on screen only: its pass ended before it climbed to full. ..."

docs.title: Older runs
docs.text: A start recorded by a much older Flux is shown as written, under a notice.

docs.title: Machines
docs.text: Every loop runs on a machine: the server itself runs none. A machine is added once from the Machines page and one line run on it. A full machine runs whole loops -- this server's own host is one, added with This server's host (below) -- and a runner runs single steps: a check or stage whose needs matches its labels (an FPGA board, a licensed tool, more cores or memory) runs there, and its numbers come back as if run beside the loop (Resource hints).

docs.title: Where a loop runs
docs.text:
• A loop attached in VS Code runs on that VS Code's machine (VS Code).
  • Any other loop runs whole on a full machine its owner may use (a server machine, a group's, their own) that has what its needs ask (flow: {needs: ...} or trunk: {needs: ...}; none: any). With a full machine on this server's disk among them it runs there, in place.
  • No machine that could run it: Start is refused, "loop: no machine", until one is added. A machine that could but is away or unhealthy keeps the start queued; it runs when the machine is back. The log's start line says where it runs.
  • A loop's Chat answers and the agent that writes or revises its problem run on a machine too: the loop's VS Code machine; else the machine its run is on, or the one machine its needs match; else one of the owner's, a group's, the server's. None: "loop: no machine". Chat about no loop, logins and agents' Test are the server's: they need no machine.

docs.title: Whose machine it is
docs.text:
A server machine A group's machine Your own machine Added by an admin an admin or one of the group's managers any user Used by every user's loops the loops of the group's members only the loops you own: never a loop shared with you, never anyone else's Added in Admin › Runtime › Machines the group's Machines tab, or Admin › Runtime › Machines (Role: A group's) Account › Machines
  • A loop uses its owner's machines, whoever starts it. A step goes to any machine its needs match; no kind is preferred.
  • A member who leaves a group (or is disabled) stops using its machines within seconds; running steps finish.
  • Deleting a group revokes its machines and cancels unused codes.
  • Machine names are unique across the server.

docs.title: What the machine needs
docs.text:
• Linux with systemd and Podman 4.9+ (cgroup v2): Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora, RHEL 9.4+. The line delegates cgroup controllers to the flux account as the server installer does (System service).
  • Nix, multi-user. The line lets flux use it and adds the binary caches (cache.nixos.org, nixchip0.cachix.org), as the server installer does.
  • Network to the Flux server and the public Nix caches. No Git, repository access or credentials.

Run the line with sudo. It installs the runner as the system service flux-worker under the flux account. If something is missing it says what and stops; run it again after.

docs.title: The Machines page
docs.text:
• Admin › Runtime › Machines: every machine (server, group, user).
  • A group's Machines tab (#/groups/<id>/machines): that group's.
  • Account › Machines: yours, the VS Code extension to download and your VS Code codes that sign it in, each used once, for every folder opened in that VS Code (VS Code), and the other machines your loops may use (read-only), so you know which labels to ask for.

Each shows:

  • Totals: cores, memory, devices (fpga=1), and use, over every machine the page shows -- VS Code and full machines too (a storage machine runs nothing): on Admin every machine, on a group's tab its machines, on Account the machines you own. "1 unhealthy" flags a machine taking no steps.
  • A row per machine: labels (× removes, + adds: lab, fpga=1, board=zcu104), use (2/16 cores, 8/56 GB), health (healthy, unhealthy with why, setting up or updating with progress, draining or drained, away after five silent minutes), running steps, Flux version (old when behind), last heard. Menu: Rename, Drain/Resume, Rotate keys, Revoke.
  • This server's host: a full machine like any other, tagged shared disk -- its loops run in their own folders, nothing copied. The server itself is no row: it runs no loop.
  • A VS Code machine: one per VS Code (desktop, code-server or a remote host each count as one), named by the code that signed it in, tagged VS Code. Its Loops column names the loops attached there, a chip each with a dot in the loop's state; click it for the list: each loop linked, running (with the cores, memory and steps its run holds there, and for how long), idle (its folder open in a VS Code window) or folder not open (the loop lives there, but no window has its folder open: its Start and its Chat here wait). No labels and no Drain; offline when it is off (not heard for 45 s), which is no fault -- the same moment its loops' Start and Chat here are refused; updating while it runs other code than the server's (its extension fetches the server's Flux and moves to it between runs: nothing to do there). Revoke signs that VS Code out and refuses its machine's key; its loops stay yours on the server, and a new sign-in and Attach there run them again under the same name.
  • A VS Code signed in with no machine yet (no folder attached): a row tagged VS Code · no machine, with Revoke (signs it out).
  • Waiting: steps no machine has taken, and why.
  • Codes not used yet, with Cancel.

+ Add machine (admins pick the Role -- Runner, Full, This server's host, Storage -- and whose: the server's, a user's, a group's) or + Add my machine: a name and labels, then the line to run, with Copy (and a hash-checked form for plain HTTP).

Labels set on the page replace earlier ones. A user's machine's labels are set only by that user; admins can still drain or revoke it. Group machine changes are audited (group machine).

docs.title: The line
docs.text:
+ Add machine (or + Add my machine) makes a one-time code and shows the line to run on the new machine, with Copy:

curl -fsSL http://flux.example.org:8765/worker/install.sh | sudo sh -s -- 'fx1-…@…'
  • The code works once, for one hour.
  • The line checks Podman and Nix, makes the flux account, joins, gets Flux from the server, prepares tools (~2 GB the first time), tests a container, and starts the flux-worker service. The machine's row shows its progress (setting up).
  • Files: /var/lib/flux-worker; cache: /var/cache/flux-worker.
  • Run it again (no code needed) to repair or change options; it keeps the machine's identity.
  • Over plain HTTP, use the page's hash-checked form.
  • Options after the code: --label KEY=VALUE (repeat), --jobs N (steps at once, default 2).

docs.title: A machine added before the system service
docs.text: A machine whose runner was a user service takes no steps. Revoke it, remove its user service on the machine, and add it again with a new code.

docs.title: Labels and needs
docs.text:
flow:
  measure:
    board:
      run: "{python} {home}/on_board.py {artifact}"
      metrics: [latency]
      needs: {fpga: true, board: zcu104}
needs Matches key: true The machine has the label A number (fpga: 1) Takes one of a counted resource; fpga=2 runs two such steps at once A word (board: zcu104) Exactly that value cores, memory, disk, arch, os What the machine measures itself (not settable by label)
  • Design's run, the baseline's, a search's run and the scope's commands take needs too. Agent work runs where the loop runs.
  • The whole loop: needs in its mode block (flow: {needs: {bigmem: true}} or trunk: {needs: ...}) picks the full machine it runs on (Where a loop runs). The log's start line says where.
  • Set labels in the machine's row (+, ×), or with --label on the line. A label only your machine has (alice-board: true) keeps your steps there.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: Each step runs in its own Podman sandbox with the loop's sandbox settings (never above the machine's size) and the server's network policy. A step without memory in needs reserves none.

docs.title: Which machine a step goes to
docs.text:
• A free machine holding most of the step's inputs (earlier stages, input files) is preferred. A step never waits for "its" machine.
  • The user who waited longest since their last step goes first.
  • Runner cache: a quarter of the disk, at most 50 GB, least recently used evicted.

docs.title: Proxies
docs.text: The line and the runner honour HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY (set them in your shell before the line; it reads them despite sudo). Give nix-daemon the proxy too when caches need it.

docs.title: When a machine cannot run a step
docs.text: A full disk, a failed sandbox or missing tools are the machine's fault: the step returns to the queue for another machine, and this one is unhealthy until it checks itself again. A step killed for lack of memory runs once more. The machine's row shows its labels, steps and health.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text:
A machine updates itself when the server's Flux changes: it stops taking steps, gets the new Flux, prepares tools, checks itself, and restarts in seconds with the same identity. Running steps carry on (one that cannot is measured again). It shows "updating" meanwhile.

A failed update keeps the old Flux and takes no steps (unhealthy, with why); it retries after ten minutes or at the server's next update. A runner started by hand, or added before the system service, cannot update: run the line again (or re-add it).

docs.title: Drain a machine
docs.text: Drain in its row: it finishes running steps and takes no new ones. Resume puts it back. Owners can drain their own machines.

docs.title: A full machine
docs.text:
A full machine runs whole loops, not single steps: every loop runs on one (Where a loop runs); one whose flow: or trunk: needs name labels runs on a full machine that has them. Away from the server's disk it works in a copy of the loop's folder, its results coming back to the server as it goes. It runs as many loops at once as its cores and memory hold, one run per loop. Admins: + Add machine, Role Full; its line ends in --role full. Shown with a Full tag.

Agent logins. A loop worked by a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) runs on a full machine whose jobs run in the sandbox: the server lends the machine the loop owner's login for each agent the loop uses, for that run alone -- kept in memory on the machine, mounted read-only into the run's sandbox, and gone when the run ends. While a login is lent, the run's network goes through the sandbox's proxy with an allowlist of its own -- each agent's own endpoint (or, with none, its kind's service: api.anthropic.com, chatgpt.com, ...), the agent's Allowed hosts (Admin › Agents, Account › Agents), the document's hosts: for it, the admin's sandbox allowlist, the loop's extra hosts, the Flux server -- and the agent's token host refused by name, so only the server ever refreshes the token (two copies refreshing would log each other out); the server refreshes Codex's before lending it. A turn the endpoint refuses for its login is lent the login again (refreshed on the server) and tried once more, once. The row says holds N logins while a run holds some (whose, for which loop). One machine holds a login at a time: a second run of yours using the same agent waits for it, its Start saying so. Logging in again on the server withdraws a lent login at once; the run's agent is logged out there. A full machine that runs its jobs on its host (its worker's FLUX_SANDBOX=0) is lent nothing and takes no such loop. Claude Code's login is a token kept as your setting, which travels with the run's variables as before; a VS Code machine brings its own logins.

docs.title: This server's host
docs.text:
The server's own computer can be such a machine too: + Add machine, Role This server's host. Its line ends in --role full --data <the server's data>; run it as root on the server itself. The worker runs under the server's account and proves it shares the server's disk, so its loops run in place, in their own folders: nothing is copied, and their agents' sessions and logins are the ones on the server. Shown with Full and shared disk tags. A loop prefers the machine of its last run for half a minute, so sessions resume there.

An update adds nothing by itself: a server whose loops ran on it before has them still, their records and logs as they were, and Start says "loop: no machine" until the host (or another full machine) is added. The system service installs the host's worker with install-service.py --with-worker (System service).

docs.title: A storage machine
docs.text:
A storage machine caches loop files for the runners: each file comes from the server once. It runs no steps.

Admins: + Add machine, Role Storage. Its line ends in --role storage.

  • Needs Nix and the network, no Podman.
  • Runners reach it on port 8766. Options: --listen HOST:PORT (default 0.0.0.0:8766), --url URL (default http://<its name>:8766).
  • Keeps files unused for a week at most, within half its disk.
  • While it is down, runners fetch from the server.
  • Shown with a Storage tag.

docs.title: Rotate a machine's keys
docs.text: Rotate keys in its row (admins for any, you for yours). New keys at the next heartbeat; the old ones stop working. No new join code. The row says "new keys asked" until done.

docs.title: Rename a machine
docs.text: Rename in its row (admins for any, this server included; you for yours). Names: lower-case letters, digits, ., _, -; unique among the machines joined and the pending codes. A revoked machine's name is free again for the same owner (its history keeps it); another owner's revoked name stays taken. Same machine: keys, labels and steps stay. Past results keep the old name.

docs.title: Remove a machine
docs.text: Revoke in its row: its key is refused from now on, and the steps it holds go back to the queue. On the machine, disable the flux-worker service and remove its unit, /var/lib/flux-worker and /var/cache/flux-worker.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: A loop's Results tab holds every design measured across all starts. The decision is on one line above three views: Designs, Graphs, Ideas. Library digests are under Files › Library.

docs.title: Designs
docs.text:
Five tabs, each with a count. Results opens on Accepted -- on All while no design is accepted yet -- and then on the tab you picked last; the address names the tab (…/results?tab=failed) and the open design (…/results?design=NAME).

Tab Holds All Every design handed in: accepted, rejected, failed and pending (the Graphs draw the accepted and rejected, whose numbers count) Accepted Checked and measured; every limit met at the judging stage Rejected Measured but missing a limit or cutoff, or rejected by a person or critic ("rejected by bob", "rejected by the critic (final)" / "(this pick)"). Never drawn on graphs. Also designs stopped at screen (cut early; their numbers muted) Failed A check refused it, or a measurement gave nothing. Shows its Checks pill (e.g. ✗ gate), the reason and when. Drafts cut by a stop end the list as "stopped before handed in" (no design, not counted) Pending Checked but not yet measured through, or re-measure pending (old numbers muted)
  • Checks pill (Failed, Pending): the deepest stage reached and its latest outcome (✓ gate, ✗ esl). Hover for every stage.
  • Latest attempt wins: if a newer attempt fails at a stage, older results past it are superseded: the design moves to Failed and its old numbers stop counting everywhere. Old attempts stay in its detail, folded.
  • A pass that tried to improve a design but made no new one ("no design") leaves the design's numbers alone.
  • Measured before a change (to the stage's command, readout, vars, input files or tools; When a measurement still counts): muted with a mark; not counted. The Overview's card offers Accept as current, Leave as stale, Re-measure -- the baseline's numbers too, when they were measured before the change (Re-measure runs pass 0 again).
  • Columns are the metrics the current attempts measured and the document names. A metric only old attempts carry leaves the lists once anything is measured again.
  • The table loads a page at a time ("32 of 300"); rows do not reshuffle while a loop runs.

docs.title: The table's tools
docs.text:
Icons at the end of the tab row:

Icon Does Star The loop's ranking (default order): decision, then rank, then objective. Click a header to sort; a third click (or the star) returns to the ranking. Empty values sort last % Relative: percent change from the latest baseline (else the accepted designs' P90, P10 when minimized, the median for an unranked metric). Hover for value and reference Eye Show hidden columns (Settings › Preferences), dimmed { } Inspect one dictionary: its entries become the columns. ✕ or None returns Two columns Compare two ticked designs: every number at every stage, the change (green better, red worse), the source diff
  • A number from an earlier stage is muted; hover says which ("· from timing").
  • A dictionary metric's column is its aggregate (its objective's, else _a, else the mean). Tick an entry in Settings › Preferences (▸) to add it as a column. Missing entries are never zero. {} raw shows every number.

docs.title: A design's detail
docs.text:
• What it misses, its numbers per stage, its idea.
  • Rationale: the design agent's own summary of its changes and why (none for a model step's design).
  • Its checks, one row per stage: the latest attempt (outcome, time, output); earlier attempts folded (2 earlier attempts); superseded stages muted.
  • Its source, notes pinned from Chat, and Reference for comparison if marked (for reading only; not the baseline).
  • Its pass opens in Live.

docs.title: Checked, not measured
docs.text: A design only checks judged shows Not measured and why (the refusing check, "its screen measurement was refused: estimated to fail", or what it waits for). Check and measure again (owner, with a reason) queues it in Pending: the running loop does it before its next pass; a loop at rest runs it now.

docs.title: Probed by agents
docs.text:
Drafts an agent probed but did not hand in end the Rejected and Failed tables under probed by agents (3), folded.

  • Named by pass and try (#p4.2; #pt1.1 under trunk t1). The agent's numbers are muted.
  • An unverified pill; hover for why ("not verified by the loop — probed by the agent only").
  • Never in graphs, the decision or standings.
  • Evaluate (owner or editor; audited) has the loop check, measure and choose it as a design: in a running flow with designs at once, at its next free lane; else at the next re-check.
  • It also leaves the list once a design with exactly its text passes Check.

docs.title: Reject a design
docs.text:
• Reject (owner, with a reason): kept and listed in Rejected with why and by whom, never chosen. Tick its numbers to re-measure or clear them.
  • A critic's rejection names the critic and what it rejected (the design, final; or this pick, which lapses when the numbers change), with Show the critic's reasoning.
  • Restore undoes every rejection on it (a person's, a critic's, a refused re-measure).
  • Check and measure again appears beside Restore after a refused re-measure. The detail says when it runs.
  • Designs hidden by hand before Nov 2026 read as rejections.

docs.title: Who made a design
docs.text: With several makers (trunks, or several Design agents), each design has a coloured tag after its number (t2, or the agent). Hover: "made by trunk t1 (claude, opus)". One maker: no tags.

docs.title: Star your key designs
docs.text:
Star (first tool in a design's head) bookmarks it. Owner and editors star; everyone who can read the loop sees stars. Each star is audited with who and when.

  • The decision has an orange trophy; a starred design an open orange star.
  • Results › Graphs draw starred points in orange (Starred in the legend). The Overview does not.
  • Stars change nothing the loop does.

docs.title: Share a design
docs.text:
Share (after Star; needs the Share right) makes a read-only link to one design: for people signed in, or anyone with the link, for 1 to 90 days (never expires: signed-in only). The dialog lists links with Copy and Revoke; Account › Shared links lists all.

The page is live and shows:

  • the design's and loop's short names, standing, trophy;
  • Measurements per stage;
  • Among the designs: on the Pareto front or how many beat it, change against the baseline; other designs only as a grey density (no numbers);
  • its idea, rationale and Checks outcomes.

Options: Include the design file (text up to 512 KB, with Download), then and its diff with the baseline (changed lines with three lines of context).

Never shared: code (unless included), check output, notes, rejection reasons, other designs' names, the loop, the library, hidden files. A revoked, expired or broken link shows This link does not open (Share).

docs.title: Invalidate, re-evaluate
docs.text:
After a check or measurement script changed, use Settings › Record:

  • Invalidate all (this loop, at rest, confirmed): sets every design aside in Pending as re-measure pending, never chosen ("40 of 40 set aside since …: re-measure pending until a re-evaluation runs"). Running it again adds only newer designs.
  • Re-Evaluate: the next start, after its baseline, re-checks and re-measures the designs of the tabs you tick ("Rejected · 143"), then runs its passes. The dialog says what it will do ("Re-checks and re-measures 12 accepted and 143 rejected designs at the next start, after its baseline").
    • Accepted, Rejected, Failed, Pending: that tab's designs now. Pending is ticked by default; Invalidate all's designs are measured only with it. All four: every design. A hand rejection stands after re-measuring.
    • Rerun baseline: pass 0 first.
    • Designs already re-measure pending are measured anyway.
    • Cancel until the start. Progress: "re-measured 12 of 40 since the invalidation at …".
    • A stop keeps what was measured ("paused: 12 of 40 done; continues at the next start").
    • A design today's checks refuse goes to Failed.

Known results are reused. A design that comes back with the same text is refused (or passed) from the record without running again: "refused here before as #N, not run again" / "passed here before as #N, not run again". An edit to the document or a file the check reads, or Re-Evaluate, runs it again.

docs.title: Graphs
docs.text:
Graph Shows Pareto front Any two metrics at the deciding stage (or a stage you pick). The pool drawn; other designs faint as excluded, each saying why ("measured on screen only: its pass ended before it climbed to full"). Decision ringed, front joined Improvement by design Best so far per metric, design by design, titled "best cycles (-12.9%)". Baselines are grey lines. Charts share one x axis

Each graph's chips:

Chip Does Stage: deepest ▾ Which stage's numbers to draw Accepted only Draw only Accepted designs Focus Fade every point off the front (Pareto) or that set no new best Zoom to an area Drag a box to zoom (flat drag: x only; upright: y only). Right-click goes back, double-click shows all, Escape cancels ⛶ Fullscreen
  • Accepted only, Focus and Zoom apply to all the loop's graphs and the Overview's, kept in your browser. Metrics, axes and stage are saved with the loop.
  • Selected design: click a point or open a row; it is an orange diamond on every graph and an orange edge in the table. Click again or Escape to clear.
  • Which way is better comes only from an objective's direction or goal (>= 300, <= 0.5). A metric no objective ranks -- one no objective names, or a tracked one (its unit kept) -- is drawn without a best line ("not an objective") and its changes are not coloured.
  • A design stopped at screen is drawn hollow.
  • Old loops with parts (from before one loop was one design): part designs are named by part (front: #3), tinted by part with a key, and never in the decision's pool.

docs.title: Ideas
docs.text:
The loop's ideas notebook: each idea and the designs that tested it.

State Pill Meaning proposed grey ring Not tested yet: no design has followed it. testing turning blue ring A design that follows it is being checked or measured now. checked green ring A design that follows it passed its checks but has no numbers yet. measured green check A design that follows it has numbers (its hover: "measured, but no sign it helped"); whether it helped is in its evidence and its score. refused red cross Every design that tested it was refused by the checks. interrupted orange bang Its last test stopped before an outcome (the loop was stopped).

Evidence: one row per design that followed the idea: the furthest stage reached, the outcome there, the numbers. Earlier tries fold in ("2 earlier tries"). A design's furthest meaningful try speaks for it; earlier failures do not count against it.

Outcome Meaning win Measured better than the standing design at that stage on some objective, by more than the noise, and worse on none. no gain Measured within the noise of the standing design on every objective. loss Measured worse beyond the noise, and better on none. tests refused A check ran and refused the design: failed tests, or a critic. This counts against the idea. checked Passed a check with no numbers yet, or a prototype that passes every input and misses the cost goal. inconclusive Says nothing about the idea: it did not build, the check did not run, the coding agent or a tool failed (a quota, a time limit, a permission), or the run stopped.
  • Noise is the objective's tie and the spread of repeated measurements. "inconclusive ×4" counts those.
  • Score ("78.7 · repeated win"; hover for parts) orders the list. Wins raise it, losses and refusals lower it, untested ideas slowly age. Kinds, best first: repeated win, single win, untested with a priority, checked, inconclusive only, untested, no gain, stale, near a refused idea, loss, refused by tests. Sort by Newest or Number instead in the State column.
  • proposed again ×3 (trunk Search buds): shown only; changes nothing.
  • Filter bar: All or one state, with counts; Marked and Deleted once used; Queued last.

docs.title: Queue
docs.text:
• The queue button on a row toggles it. Tags: next pass, queued · 2, ...
  • Each pass builds a design for the oldest queued idea until one has a meaningful outcome.
  • After three passes of only inconclusive designs it leaves the queue (Live says so): fix the setup and queue it again.
  • Queue N queues every untested idea, best first. Clear empties the queue.
  • A running loop reads the queue at its next pass.

docs.title: Merged, project and deleted ideas
docs.text:
• Ideas cleanup folds merged ideas under the kept one ("merged into idea 3").
  • An idea from a linked project's knowledge has a tag "from silicon@hw-lab" (links to the project). A retired entry marks it for deletion, unless a measured design keeps it.
  • Delete (bin; owner and editors): gone from agents and the queue. Undo, or Restore under Deleted. Text and evaluations stay on record; audited.
  • A folded row (×N) deletes all its ideas (Delete N ideas); open it to delete one.
  • Marked for deletion (by an agent, with a reason and who): the loop reads it as before until a person picks Accept (deletes, with Undo) or Reject (keeps; the same agent cannot mark it again until new evidence). Marked N filters them. Chat's agent proposes deletions for you to Accept in Chat.
